etymologyHint: Avoiding 免 the sun 日; 免 also provides the pronunciation

example.fact: China spans a huge area but uses only one official time, Beijing Time, so evening arrives at the same clock time nationwide.

etymologyHint: A container 皿 overflowing with water 水

components.note: 水 (water) — shown overflowing the rim, representing surplus or abundance

example.pinyin: Hē shuǐ duì shēntǐ hěn yǒuyì.

example.fact: About sixty percent of the human body is water, so drinking enough water each day is beneficial to health.

etymologyHint: The place 阝 of the sun 日; compare 阴

components.note: 阝 (a hillside/place) — the sunlit side of a hill or place

meanings: used in 蘭若|兰若[lan2 re3]

meanings: to send; to deliver; to transmit
etymologyHint: A person waving 关 to someone walking away 辶

example.pinyin: Sòng lǐwù de shíhou, Zhōngguórén bú sòng zhōngbiǎo.
example.english: When giving gifts, Chinese people do not give clocks.
example.fact: In Chinese, 'clock' (钟) sounds like 'the end' (终), so clocks are traditionally seen as an unlucky gift.

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 急 relates to an anxious or urgent state of mind

example.pinyin: Rén zháojí de shíhou, xīntiào huì biàn kuài.

example.fact: When a person feels anxious or urgent (着急), the body's stress response naturally speeds up the heartbeat.

etymologyHint: A chalice 皿 filled with blood 丿

components.note: 皿 (a vessel) — a chalice or bowl

example.pinyin: Zhāngyú yǒu sān gè xīnzàng, zhè ràng hěn duō rén hěn jīngyà.

etymologyHint: A silken thread 糸 hanging off a tree 龶

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 艺 originally related to planting and cultivating skillfully
乙 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 艺's reading yì, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 中国书法是一种传统艺术。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó shūfǎ shì yì zhǒng chuántǒng yìshù.
example.english: Chinese calligraphy is a traditional art form.
example.fact: Chinese calligraphy, practiced for thousands of years, is recognized by UNESCO as part of humanity's cultural heritage.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 背 refers to the back, a part of the body

example.hanzi: 中国学生从小就要背诵唐诗。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó xuésheng cóngxiǎo jiù yào bèisòng Tángshī.
example.english: Chinese students have to recite Tang poems from a young age.
example.fact: Chinese students often memorize and recite classical Tang Dynasty poems (唐诗) starting from a young age.

etymologyHint: A formation 阝of soldiers 车

components.note: 阝 (a mound/formation) — soldiers arranged in position
车 (chariot) — war chariots lined up in formation

example.hanzi: 夏天常常突然下一阵大雨。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān chángcháng tūrán xià yí zhèn dà yǔ.
example.english: In summer, sudden bursts of heavy rain often fall.
example.fact: 阵 is a measure word for something that happens in a burst or spell, such as 一阵雨 ('a burst of rain') or 一阵风 ('a gust of wind').

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 草 refers to grass or plants
早 (zǎo) gives a sound close to 草's reading cǎo, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.pinyin: Nèi Měnggǔ yǒu hěn dà de cǎoyuán.
example.english: Inner Mongolia has vast grasslands.
example.fact: Inner Mongolia is home to vast grasslands that have supported nomadic herding for thousands of years.

meanings: leg (of an animal or an object)

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脚 refers to the foot, a part of the body

example.pinyin: Rén de yì zhī jiǎo dàyuē yǒu èrshíliù kuài gǔtou.
example.english: One human foot has about twenty-six bones.
example.fact: Each human foot contains about twenty-six bones — roughly a quarter of all the bones in the entire body.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 概 originally referred to a wooden leveling bar used to strike excess grain off a measure, later extended to 'in general, roughly'
既 (jì) gives a sound distantly related to 概's reading gài, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 地球大概有四十六亿年的历史。
example.pinyin: Dìqiú dàgài yǒu sìshíliù yì nián de lìshǐ.
example.english: Earth is approximately 4.6 billion years old.
example.fact: Scientists estimate that Earth is approximately 4.6 billion years old, based on the age of the oldest rocks and meteorites.

meanings: used in 惡心|恶心[e3 xin1]

components.note: 心 (heart) — 恶 relates to an evil or malicious state of heart/mind
亚 (yà) gives a sound distantly related to 恶's reading è, having drifted apart over time

example.pinyin: Chīle bù xīnxiān de dōngxi, tā juéde hěn ěxīn.
example.english: After eating something not fresh, he felt nauseous.
example.fact: 恶心 (to feel nauseous) literally combines 恶 'bad, evil' with 心 'heart,' describing an unpleasant feeling in the stomach.

meanings: classifier for pieces of cloth, cake, soap etc
(coll.) classifier for money and currency units

components.note: 土 (earth/soil) — 块 originally referred to a lump or clod of earth
夬 (guài) gives a sound distantly related to 块's reading kuài, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 在中国,人们口语里常说'一块钱',书面语是'一元'。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, rénmen kǒuyǔ lǐ cháng shuō 'yí kuài qián', shūmiànyǔ shì 'yì yuán'.
example.english: In China, people usually say 'yí kuài qián' in spoken language, while the written form is 'yì yuán.'
example.fact: In spoken Chinese, 块 (kuài) is the everyday word for the basic unit of currency, while 元 (yuán) is used in writing and formal contexts.

components.note: 页 (head) — 顿 originally related to bowing the head, i.e. a pause or stop
屯 (tún) gives a sound distantly related to 顿's reading dùn, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 中国人一天通常吃三顿饭。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguórén yì tiān tōngcháng chī sān dùn fàn.
example.english: Chinese people usually eat three meals a day.
example.fact: 顿 is the measure word for meals in Chinese, as in 一顿饭 ('one meal'); most people traditionally eat three meals a day.

etymologyHint: A hand with a stick 攵 striking a beast 耳

components.note: 耳 — a wild beast being confronted
攵 (a hand with a stick) — striking at the beast, showing boldness

example.hanzi: 郑和敢率领船队远航到非洲。
example.pinyin: Zhèng Hé gǎn shuàilǐng chuánduì yuǎnháng dào Fēizhōu.
example.english: Zheng He dared to lead fleets on long voyages to Africa.
example.fact: Ming Dynasty admiral Zheng He led massive fleets on long ocean voyages that reached as far as East Africa, six hundred years ago.

etymologyHint: Keeping something 寸 within one's walls 宀

components.note: 宀 (walls/roof) — the boundary of a home to be protected
寸 (a hand) — keeping watch, holding the space within the walls

example.hanzi: 长城是古代用来防守的建筑。
example.pinyin: Chángchéng shì gǔdài yònglái fángshǒu de jiànzhù.
example.english: The Great Wall was an ancient structure built for defense.
example.fact: The Great Wall was originally built as a defensive structure to guard against invasions from the north.

etymologyHint: A jar 酉 of wine 氵; 酉 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 酉 (a wine jar) — the vessel holding the drink
氵 (liquid) — the wine itself inside the jar

example.hanzi: 白酒是中国传统的酒。
example.pinyin: Báijiǔ shì Zhōngguó chuántǒng de jiǔ.
example.english: Baijiu is a traditional Chinese liquor.
example.fact: Baijiu, a strong traditional Chinese liquor, is one of the most widely consumed distilled spirits in the world.

etymologyHint: A bird 鸟 perched atop a mountain 山

components.note: 鸟 (a bird) — a bird resting
山 (a mountain) — the mountain peak the bird perches on, rising from the sea

example.hanzi: 海南岛是中国最大的海岛。
example.pinyin: Hǎinán Dǎo shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de hǎidǎo.
example.english: Hainan Island is China's largest island.
example.fact: Hainan is China's largest island, known for its tropical climate and beaches.

meanings: to hold up in one's hand; to support with one's palm
sth serving as a support: a prop, a rest (e.g. arm rest)
etymologyHint: Using one's hands 扌 for support 乇; 乇 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support

example.hanzi: 坐飞机的时候,大件行李要托运。
example.pinyin: Zuò fēijī de shíhou, dàjiàn xínglǐ yào tuōyùn.
example.english: When flying, large luggage must be checked in.
example.fact: When flying, large pieces of luggage must be checked in (托运) rather than carried onto the plane.

example.hanzi: 中央电视台是中国最大的电视台。
example.pinyin: Zhōngyāng Diànshìtái shì Zhōngguó zuì dà de diànshìtái.
example.english: China Central Television is China's largest television station.
example.fact: China Central Television (中央电视台), whose name uses 央 for 'central,' is the country's largest state broadcaster.

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 戶; a door swinging on its hinge

components.note: 户 (a simplified form of 戶) depicts a single door panel swinging on its hinge.

example.hanzi: 中国的户口制度影响人们住在哪里。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó de hùkǒu zhìdù yǐngxiǎng rénmen zhù zài nǎlǐ.
example.english: China's household registration system affects where people can live.
example.fact: China's household registration system, called 户口 (hùkǒu), has historically influenced where people can live, work, and access public services.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 烈 relates to something as intense and fierce as fire

example.hanzi: 奥运会的比赛常常非常激烈。
example.pinyin: Àoyùnhuì de bǐsài chángcháng fēicháng jīliè.
example.english: Olympic competitions are often extremely intense.
example.fact: At the Olympics, athletes who have trained for years often compete in extremely intense (激烈) matches decided by fractions of a second.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洋 refers to the vast ocean
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 洋's reading yáng

example.hanzi: 太平洋是世界上最大的海洋。
example.pinyin: Tàipíngyáng shì shìjiè shàng zuì dà de hǎiyáng.
example.english: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
example.fact: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth, covering about one-third of the planet's surface.

etymologyHint: One person talking 可 over another 可

components.note: 哥 doubles the character 可 ('to approve, to sing'), originally suggesting a call-and-response song between two singers; the meaning later narrowed to 'elder brother.'

example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó chuántǒng jiātíng lǐ, gēge chángcháng yào zhàogù dìdi mèimei.
example.english: In traditional Chinese families, older brothers often look after their younger siblings.
example.fact: 哥 (elder brother) doubles the character 可, which may originally have suggested a call-and-response song between two singers.

etymologyHint: A rope 糸 hanging from the ceiling 冖

components.note: 糸 (thread) — thick strands twisted into a rope
冖 (a covering) — the ceiling or beam the rope hangs from

example.hanzi: 黄山有很长的索道,可以带游客上山。
example.pinyin: Huángshān yǒu hěn cháng de suǒdào, kěyǐ dài yóukè shàng shān.
example.english: Mount Huangshan has a long cableway that can carry visitors up the mountain.
example.fact: Mount Huangshan in China has a long cableway (索道) that carries visitors up its steep, scenic peaks.

meanings: non-Han people, esp. from central Asia

components.note: ⺼ (flesh) — 胡 originally referred to the flesh under an animal's chin or throat

example.pinyin: Běijīng yǒu hěn duō lǎo hútòng.
example.english: Beijing has many old hutong alleys.
example.fact: Beijing's hutongs (胡同) are narrow traditional alleyways that have existed since imperial times, some over seven hundred years old.

components.note: 欠 (to owe/lack) — 款 relates to funds, especially money owed or paid

example.pinyin: Hěn duō Zhōngguórén xǐhuan bǎ qián cún zài yínháng lǐ, jiàozuò cúnkuǎn.
example.english: Many Chinese people like to keep their money in the bank, called savings.
example.fact: China has traditionally had one of the highest household savings rates in the world.

meanings: to stand by the side of

example.pinyin: Xióngmāo de shēngcún zhǔyào kào zhúzi.
example.english: Pandas' survival mainly relies on bamboo.
example.fact: Giant pandas rely almost entirely on bamboo for food, even though their digestive system is better suited to eating meat.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 评 relates to speaking judgments or opinions about something
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 评's reading píng

example.hanzi: 很多人喜欢在网上写评价。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén xǐhuan zài wǎngshàng xiě píngjià.
example.english: Many people like to write reviews online.
example.fact: 评价 (to evaluate, a review) combines 评 'to judge, comment' with 价 'value' — literally, judging something's value.

components.note: 片 (a slice/plate) — 版 originally referred to a wooden printing block
反 (fǎn) gives the sound — an exact match with 版's reading bǎn

example.hanzi: 中国古代发明了木版印刷术。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó gǔdài fāmíngle mùbǎn yìnshuāshù.
example.english: Ancient China invented woodblock printing.
example.fact: Ancient China invented woodblock printing, one of the earliest forms of printing in the world, over a thousand years ago.

etymologyHint: Jade 玉 kept in one's house 宀

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — a house where valuables are kept
玉 (jade) — the treasure kept safe inside

example.english: The Palace Museum houses many national treasures.
example.fact: The Palace Museum in Beijing, located in the former Forbidden City, houses an enormous collection of Chinese national treasures.

meanings: (archaic) suffix used in a respectful form of address (e.g. 師座|师座[shi1 zuo4])
etymologyHint: A wide 广 seat 坐; 坐 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 广 (a wide, open building) — a hall or pavilion
坐 (to sit) — a seat placed inside the building

example.fact: China's 'Five Great Mountains' (五岳) have been sacred sites for religious pilgrimage and imperial ceremony for over two thousand years.

meanings: Buddha (abbr. for 釋迦牟尼|释迦牟尼[Shi4 jia1 mou2 ni2])

example.english: China has programs to release captive-bred pandas into the wild.
example.fact: China has programs that release captive-bred pandas (释放) back into the wild to help boost the species' population.

etymologyHint: The sun 日 rising over a city 京; 京 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 日 (the sun) — sunlight falling over the land
京 (a capital city) — a grand city view worth seeing

example.hanzi: 桂林的风景非常美。
example.pinyin: Guìlín de fēngjǐng fēicháng měi.

example.fact: Guilin, in southern China, is famous for its dramatic karst mountain scenery along the Li River.

meanings: to look after; to take into consideration; to attend to

components.note: 页 (head) — 顾 originally related to turning the head to look back at something
厄 (è) gives a sound distantly related to 顾's reading gù, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 在中国,老人通常由家人照顾。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, lǎorén tōngcháng yóu jiārén zhàogù.
example.english: In China, elderly people are usually cared for by their family.

example.hanzi: 在中国传统家庭里,弟弟要尊重哥哥。
example.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó chuántǒng jiātíng lǐ, dìdi yào zūnzhòng gēge.

example.fact: In traditional Chinese family culture, birth order carries importance, with younger siblings like 弟弟 (younger brother) traditionally expected to show respect to their elders.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — 登 relates to climbing or ascending with one's legs
豆 (dòu) gives a sound distantly related to 登's reading dēng, having drifted apart over time

example.pinyin: Hěn duō Zhōngguórén xǐhuan dēng Tàishān kàn rìchū.
example.english: Many Chinese people like to climb Mount Tai to see the sunrise.
example.fact: Mount Tai, one of China's most sacred mountains, has attracted pilgrims and climbers for thousands of years, many hiking through the night to see the sunrise from its summit.

components.note: 贝 (shell/money) — 货 relates to goods that are bought and sold for money
化 (huà) gives a sound distantly related to 货's reading huò, having drifted apart over time

example.english: The Port of Shanghai is one of the busiest cargo ports in the world.
example.fact: The Port of Shanghai is one of the busiest cargo ports in the world, handling an enormous volume of goods each year.

components.note: 互 depicts two hooked or interlocking shapes, holding onto each other to show mutual connection.

example.english: The internet has changed people's lives.
example.fact: 互联网 (the internet) literally means 'mutually connected network' — combining 互 'mutually' with 联 'connected' and 网 'net.'

etymologyHint: To hand 寸 something over to someone 亻

components.note: 亻 (a person) — someone receiving something
寸 (a hand) — a hand handing something over
